content.text:
I built the Markdown-to-HTML renderer in `src/markdown.js`, and `node --test` passes all 12 tests: the public smoke test plus 11 of my own in `tests/unit/markdown.test.js`. **Retrieval decision:** I wrote it myself. The subset in SPEC.md is small and specific, and adapting commonmark.js would have meant a large vendoring job plus changing its raw-HTML handling, since the spec wants raw HTML escaped. I followed the CommonMark 0.31 algorithms directly. No code was copied, so `PROVENANCE.json` is `[]` and `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` says nothing is vendored. **What it handles:** - **Blocks:** ATX headings, paragraphs (newlines kept inside them), fenced code blocks with a `language-x` class, blockquotes (including continuation lines without `>`), and thematic breaks. - **Lists:** `-`, `*` and `+` bullets and ordered lists, with `start` when they don't begin at 1. Tight lists render without `

` inside items, and loose ones are detected too. - **Inline:** code spans, backslash escapes, hard line breaks, emphasis and strong (no intraword `_`), links and images with titles, and percent-encoding of link URLs the way commonmark.js does it. - **Escaping:** `& < > "` are escaped everywhere, and raw HTML is always output as escaped text. - **Beyond the subset:** setext headings, indented code blocks and autolinks, because commonmark.js would produce them. Only a small table of common named entities is decoded (e.g. `©`); numeric ones are all handled. **Check against the official spec:** I ran it on 416 examples from CommonMark 0.31.2, from the sections this subset covers, skipping any that use raw HTML or reference-style links. 413 match commonmark.js output. The 3 mismatches are edge cases: - a tab right after a backslash comes out as spaces; - a `===` line after a continuation line inside a blockquote becomes a heading instead of paragraph text; - a nested list item followed by a blank line and then more text isn't marked loose. I used that spec file only for this local check; it isn't part of the deliverable.
